symptom: `rest call … returns mapping M.IMM as Module.Entity` builds cleanly — `mxcli check`, `mx check` 0 errors, mxbuild fine — and throws the moment the activity runs, over a valid response body: `MicroflowException: key not found: Path(QName(None,),None,)` at `MappingCache.storeValueMappingElement`. `as list of` instead fails the BUILD with CE0243, so an object-rooted mapping has no working `returns mapping` form at all
cause: The REST branch mirrored BOTH of the ImportMappingCall's flags onto the result variable's cardinality. They are three axes, not one: `SingleObject` types the VARIABLE, `ForceSingleOccurrence` means "the mapping yields many, bind one", `Range.SingleObject` is Studio Pro's First/All. `as Entity` set all three true, so an OBJECT-rooted mapping was told to force an occurrence it does not have. #192 fixed the identical conflation in the sibling `import from mapping` branch and never reached this one
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_calls.go` (`addRestCallAction`'s `ast.RestResultMapping` case + the shared `mappingRootIsList` helper); tests `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_rest_mapping_occurrence_test.go`; example `mdl-examples/bug-tests/242-rest-mapping-single-object-runtime.mdl`
insight: **Measure the flags one at a time before fixing.** All four combinations were run in one boot over the same mapping and JSON: `FSO=true/Range=true` FAIL, `FSO=true/Range=false` FAIL, `FSO=false/Range=false` PASS, `FSO=false/Range=true` PASS — so `ForceSingleOccurrence` alone drives the exception and `Range` is innocent, which is NOT what reading the code suggests. **Do not write `ForceSingleOccurrence=false` unconditionally**: that fixes the object-rooted case and silently strips the flag from `PrivateCloudData.REST_GetEnvironmentByUUID`, a Studio Pro document that binds one object out of a LIST-rooted mapping and stores it true (recorded in `mdl-examples/bug-tests/519-rest-mapping-as-list-of.mdl`). Infer it from the MAPPING's root instead — true only when the mapping yields many AND the call site binds one. An unresolvable mapping must read as object-rooted: guessing "list" fails at RUN time, guessing "object" is caught by mxbuild as CE0243 at BUILD time. **A unit test on the flags is not enough** — every static check passes on the broken document, so the regression example has to be driven through `mxcli test --local` with a real JSON endpoint (`python3 -m http.server`), and the generated test wrapper swallows the exception text: call `MxTest.Test_*` directly through `/mxtest/run` with the token from `<project>/.mxcli/test-endpoint.json` to read it.
